title: Statement Regarding the Publication of Reference Rates on Friday, April 3, 2026

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: The New York Fed announced that TGCR, BGCR, SOFR, and SOFR Averages will not be published on Friday, April 3, 2026 (Good Friday), due to repo market participants broadly expecting to treat that date as a holiday. Settlement of cleared Treasury repo will not be available, eliminating two of three market segments used to calculate these Treasury repo reference rates. EFFR and OBFR will continue to publish on April 3 as they follow the NY Fed's own holiday schedule.
key_points: TGCR, BGCR, SOFR, and SOFR Averages/Index will not publish on April 3, 2026
EFFR and OBFR will publish on April 3, 2026 (follow NY Fed holiday schedule)
Cleared Treasury repo settlement unavailable on April 3, eliminating two of three segments for TGCR/BGCR/SOFR
SIFMA did not recommend full closure of US government securities trading due to March Employment Situation report release
On April 6, TGCR, BGCR, and SOFR will publish reflecting same-day settling repo transactions settling Thursday April 2 and maturing Monday April 6
why_it_matters: Market participants relying on SOFR-based instruments, derivatives pricing, or lending benchmarks need to know that Friday April 3 reference rates will be unavailable. This affects any contracts, valuations, or risk systems that depend on continuous SOFR publication. The gap in published SOFR values means market participants should plan for alternative data handling or pricing adjustments during this period.
market_structure_context: This statement documents how reference rate publication adapts to market holiday schedules. The split treatment—EFFR/OBFR published but TGCR/BGCR/SOFR suspended—reflects the different holiday conventions across federal funds, bank funding, and Treasury repo markets. The suspension of cleared repo settlement directly impacts the three-segment calculation methodology for Treasury GC rates.
notes: Source is a formal operating policy statement from the NY Fed. Published March 12, 2026, approximately 7 weeks before the affected date (April 3, 2026). This is a forward-looking notice about market operations rather than historical data. The statement is highly relevant to market structure as it details the mechanics of reference rate publication under non-standard market conditions.
